**Early access / beta.** Finca Animate is a free, open-source 2D animation studio for Linux and Windows, inspired by Toon Boom Harmony. It's based on [OpenToon Studio](https://github.com/helliott20/opentoon) by helliott20 and contributors (MIT). This is a personal project, shared as-is: things will change, and support is best-effort.

## Download

**Linux:** download `Finca-Animate-1.1.0-beta.3-x86_64.AppImage`, right-click it, open Properties, allow executing as a program, then double-click it. If it doesn't start, your system may be missing `libfuse2`: install that, or use the `.tar.gz` instead (extract it and run `opentoon-studio` inside).

**Windows:** download `Finca-Animate-Setup-1.1.0-beta.3.exe` and run it. The installer isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen will show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

Already on beta.2? The app will offer this update (on Linux, only after you approve it). Read **Please note** first: projects now save in a new format.

## What's new since beta.2

**Storyboard mode**
- File → New Storyboard (or the Storyboard template) starts a Storyboard Pro style board: a strip of panels across the top with scene / panel numbers, durations and captions, panels you can reorder by dragging, and + Panel, Duplicate, Delete and + Scene.
- Each panel has a duration, a transition, dialogue, action notes and notes. Drawing on a layer fills the whole panel, so each panel shows one drawing per layer.
- Panels show on the timeline. Press Enter to play the animatic, export it as a movie, or export a PDF storyboard: 3 panels per page with captions beside them, 6 per page, or 1 per page, on Letter or A4.
- The Animate | Storyboard switch at the top right goes back to plain animation and keeps every panel and caption.

**A new project format: `.finca`**
- Projects save as one self-contained `.finca` file, faster to save and open on big scenes, with drawings stored once and loaded as needed.
- Saves are safer: the backup is never half-written, a full disk or a failed background save is reported, and a file cut short by a crash still opens with what it holds.
- `.otoon` projects still open; saving one asks for a new `.finca` file.
- Render from the command line: `opentoon-studio --render scene.finca -o out.mp4`.

**Themes**
- View → Theme: Harmony Graphite, Paper (light), Classic, and Follow FZ Theme. On a Finca Zero desktop the app takes the desktop theme's colours and artwork and changes with it live; elsewhere it uses Classic.

**Drawing with a pen**
- A tool properties bar across the top of the stage: the tool in hand, its size, opacity, smoothing and brush presets.
- A pie menu of tools: tap the pen's side button on the canvas, or press Q.
- Smoothing works like Photoshop's: the brush follows your path while you draw, and the line is rebuilt smooth when you lift. Ovals drawn freehand come out round; a stroke that ends where it began closes cleanly.
- Layers and storyboard panels can be dragged with a pen. Drag empty space in a panel or list, or hold the side button and drag, to scroll.
- Drawing over an erased spot works again.
- Toolbar tooltips show the keys that really pick each tool.

## Please note

- **Projects now save as `.finca`, which beta.2 can't open.** If you might go back to beta.2, keep a copy of your `.otoon` files.
- **Back up anything important.** This is a beta.
- Follow FZ Theme only does something on a Finca Zero desktop; Windows and other Linux desktops get the Classic look unless you pick another theme.
